narrative_purpose: Shows the shared specification holding across living, fleshed Pandoran animals of very different trades - the count of six limbs, four eyes, paired temple queues recurs no matter the body shape, driving home that this is inheritance, not chance.
subject: A naturalist line-up of four living Pandoran animals of clearly different kinds - a tall grazing direhorse-like quadrupedal-looking beast that on close look has six legs, a low six-legged viperwolf-like hunter, a perched winged flyer, and a heavy hammerhead-browed herbivore - each posed in profile, each subtly showing the same six limbs, four eyes, and the pair of fine neural braids at the temples.
scene: A glowing forest clearing at night, the four animals arranged across it at different depths, bioluminescent flora hazing the background.
camera: A wide naturalist field view taking in all four animals, foreground ones larger, the far ones softened by haze.
light: Bioluminescent ambient glow from surrounding flora, cyan and teal, catching the animals' eyes and temple-braids; deep indigo shadow.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal ground, cyan and living-teal biolum on flora and eyes, scarce magenta blooms, restrained warm accent.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, field-survey clarity.
detail_level: Crisp on each animal's limb count, eyes, and temple-braids; background flora soft; far animals dissolving into haze.
composition: Four animals staggered across the frame at varied depth, eyes and queues catching the light, generous dark canopy negative space above.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette, bioluminescent key. Animals read as kin of one family despite different trades. Same mood as the chapter cover.
